answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by capping rewards per bonded stake, not per identity. Picture an orchard where each tree is one bonded public key: it must lock its own non-transferable deposit, which cannot be split, shared, or reused by another identity. A farm that plants a hundred lotus lookalikes still faces the same ceiling, because each extra fake must post a fresh full deposit and wait out the same lock, while a quartz-clear audit forfeits the deposit of any identity caught copying another's work. Splitting buys no extra yield, only extra locked capital and time.
